newsitem.title: INDONESIA: SE Asian Grain - Corn slips in Indonesia on harvest.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Grain - Corn slips in Indonesia on harvest.

text.p: Corn prices came under harvest pressure in Indonesia this week, but were largely steady in other Southeast Asian markets with the picture in soymeal broadly similar, regional traders said on Wednesday.

Ample domestic stocks and the early stages of the harvest in the key growing region of Lampung saw Jakarta corn prices quoted at between 400-405 rupiah a kg compared with 415-420 rupiah a week ago, traders said.
Traders said daily arrivals of corn in Lampung were still relatively small at about 50 tonnes, adding that arrivals could reach up to 2,000 tonnes daily in January.
"The harvest is proceeding slowly, and I expect it to gather speed next month ahead of the peak in January," one trader said. "Prices are beginning to weaken because of the harvest."
"There has been no news of imports as buyers are mostly covered until the end of the year," another trader said. "They are now looking at first quarter (1997) imports."
Domestic Indonesian soymeal prices were unchanged at between 800-810 rupiah/kg amid plentiful local supplies.
In Thailand, soymeal prices were mostly stable this week as more supplies are coming into the market later in the month, trade sources said. Corn prices were also steady in moderate trade, they said.
Despite forecasts of bullish demand for soymeal next year, no buyers have placed orders to cover next year's demand as soybean prices remain high and the demand for 1996 has been fully covered.
Domestic Thai soymeal was quoted at around 9.60 baht ($0.38) and corn at 4.30-4.40 baht a kg, barely changed from last week, the trade sources said.
"There's no activity in the market. The industry sees no rush to buy at the moment," one trader said.
"Local soymeal prices could ease next week as more supplies are seen coming to the market,' he added.
About 20,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal is expected to arrive in Thailand on Saturday and 45,000 tonnes more will arrive on Monday, according to shipping sources.
The Thai animal feed industry forecast that the demand for soymeal in 1997 could reach 1.7 million tonnes from between 1.3-1.4 million tonnes expected this year.
Of the total, more than one million tonnes are expected to be directly imported, they said.
The industry predicted that about 670,000 tonnes of soymeal will be produced domestically from soybeans, both local and imported, by oil crushers for oil extraction.
In Malaysia, local grain prices were unchanged this week with buyers still watching the sliding Chicago futures market.

A purchase of 30,000 tonnes of South American soymeal at $240 tonne C&F for May 1997 shipment by a consortium of four Malaysian feedmillers was the only substantial business reported in the whole of last week, traders said.
The consignment of low-protein soymeal ordered by See Hoy Chan, Ho Seng Chan, QL Feedstuff and Gold Coin Bhd will arrive in June, the traders said.
"There's still not much incentive for buying as consumers are well-stocked for the first quarter of 1997," said a trader.
Bulk corn for December was being offered at between 475 to 480 ringgit a tonne ex-factory/godown in the central region.
"A" grade wheat in bags was indicated at 800 ringgit a tonne ex-factory/godown in the central region while low-grade wheat was maintained at 500 to 510 ringgit on the same basis
Local soymeal was quoted at 810 ringgit a tonne while imported soymeal was going for about 800 ringgit.
